children: Hedge funds reduced their short positions in the yen and increased bullish bets on the Australian dollar in the week through October 20. According to Sina Finance, citing data released Friday by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), short bets against the euro reached their highest level since 2020; funds also became more bullish on the pound and Australian dollar and more bearish on the Canadian dollar, whose net short position reached its highest level since early August. The yen rose for a second consecutive week but edged lower against the U.S. dollar on Friday. As of October 20, hedge funds, asset managers and other speculators held less than $40 billion in positions betting on a stronger dollar, down from $44.5 billion the previous week, based on CFTC data and calculations.

title: CFTC: Hedge Funds Cut Yen Shorts and Increase Australian Dollar Longs
